properties.decision: One PR, two changes. (1) reflow2-mcp gets its own `rocksdb` feature, ON by default, so every build anyone installs or runs is unchanged; one short cargo command builds and tests without it on the in-memory BTreeMap backend, and AGENTS.md makes that the local gate; a build without it refuses a store in a folder with a message naming the fix; tests that need the disk run only with it; CI's full job keeps it on and runs every test on every PR, and CI also builds the configuration without it so it cannot rot. (2) The server crate's ~171 integration test files compile into a few test programs (`autotests = false`, explicit `[[test]]` targets pulling the files in with `#[path]`), the files staying where they are so every Artifact and Verification naming them stays valid; tests that share process state (environment, current directory, fixed paths) stay isolated. reflow2-core's 224 test files are consolidated the same way: Anthony's word came 2026-10-15 ("Yes, consolidate reflow2-core's tests"). The same pattern — `autotests = false`, explicit `[[test]]` targets with `#[path]`, files staying where they are — split by feature: a no-features program (the bulk), a `rocksdb` program, a `fulltext` program, and isolated programs for tests with process-wide state.
properties.name: RocksDB becomes a default-on feature of the server crate, everyday work builds without it, and the server's tests compile into a few programs
properties.rationale:
Anthony, 2026-10-15: "for the vast majority of development, I don't think it's necessary" and "Go with your 1 PR and two changes". MEASURED that day on origin/main e45225520 and in a live worktree: the core already defaults to the in-memory backend (CI's no-RocksDB core job ~3 min against ~28 for the full one); reflow2-mcp's Cargo.toml turned RocksDB on unconditionally ("the design must survive across agent sessions", a rule for the shipped server written so every build of the crate needed it), and workspace feature unification gave the core tests RocksDB too; 128 of the server's 171 test files already ran on an in-memory design; each server test program was ~390 MB, RocksDB ~9 MB of its ~52 MB of code; a debug librocksdb-sys build is 2.0 GB per copy and 10-19 min cold. The disk's bulk is the ~170 programs and cargo's lack of GC (fact:the-target-dir-reached-263-gib-of-this-projects-own-test-binaries), which is why change (2) is the larger disk lever.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT REOPEN: production stays RocksDB (dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability, ruled 2026-09-11). CI still tests on RocksDB, so the deferred CI question (dec:idea-ci-tests-on-the-in-memory-backend-unless-the-store-changes) stays deferred; this answers its noted unknown, "whether reflow2-mcp and its tests build at all without RocksDB", and the cost it named as really paid, the local build. It carries out dec:idea-a-change-runs-its-full-gate-set-once-locally-or-in-ci-not-both with a cheaper local gate. Counter-argument kept: fidelity — users run RocksDB, so disk-bound behaviour is caught only by CI's full job, and any difference between the backends found while building this is reported, never papered over.
